$comment: SPEC §7.1 / §34.3 / §2.4 — the review status of the morning-brief copy. The strings themselves live in packages/i18n/messages/{locale}.json under `terms.*` and `brief.*`, which is where every user-facing string lives (root CLAUDE.md). This file exists so `release_gates` has an artefact to read a review status off, in the same shape as the §9 safety corpora and glossary.json.

covers.terms.ordinal_house.*: 12 house ordinals per locale, as WORDS in hi/hi-Latn

reviewer_notes: ORDINALS — look here first. The first cut rendered house ordinals as digit+suffix ('{house}वें भाव'), which is wrong for houses 1 and 2: Hindi wants 'पहले भाव' and 'दूसरे भाव'. All twelve are now catalogued as words per locale (terms.ordinal_house), in the OBLIQUE form that agrees with 'भाव' in 'आपके … भाव में/से'. Please check the agreement and the spelling of पाँचवें / छठे / नौवें in particular, and the Hinglish transliterations (pehle, doosre, teesre, chauthe, paanchve, chhathe, saatve, aathve, nauve, dasve, gyarahve, barahve) — those were written by the implementer, not by a native speaker.

Changing an ordinal WORD means changing `ordinal_house_words` in chat_orchestration/policy/claim_terms.json too. The grounding validator maps the word back to a house number so §5.3's numbers-verbatim check still catches a polished line that moved a graha from the 7th house to the 1st; a form the map does not know fails closed, which is loud but is a broken gate until it is fixed.

Devanagari and Hinglish forms of the closed-set terms are standard transliterations and were not authored by a native reviewer; they are the highest-risk entries here because they are the words a devout user will notice first.

The templates deliberately carry NO fear-selling register (§9, §13): no consequence-if-you-do-not, no urgency, no prediction of harm. A reviewer changing wording must keep that property — the fear-selling lint runs on the polished output, not on these templates.
Slots are filled from FactSnapshot values only. A reviewer may reorder or reword around a slot; removing a slot changes what the sentence asserts and needs the composer changed with it.
§2.4: a term missing in a locale DROPS its module rather than falling back to English. An incomplete catalog therefore shows up as a thinner brief, never as an English sentence in a Hindi brief.
